title: רמי בר חמא

paragraphs: Rami bar Hama. Rav Avya married his sister (see there; needs examination). Amemar was his daughter's son (see there). In Rashi, Ketubbot 21, beginning of b, it is impossible to say Rami bar Hama testified about Amemar and Rav Ashi, since Rav Ashi was several generations later: Rav Ashi was born on the day Rava died. He spoke in Rav Assi’s name (Eruvin 100b). Rav Ashi married his daughter (see there; needs examination). He spoke in Rav Huna’s name (Eruvin 5a). Rav Huna came to Argiza; his host's son raised a contradiction to him, etc. He said, ‘Rami bar Hama has already resolved it’: Zevahim 18, beginning of b. Rav Hisda was his father-in-law and teacher; he asked him: Eruvin 8, end of b, 34b, 73a; Pesahim 27b; Yoma 58a; Ketubbot 86b. Yuhasin writes in a gloss, ‘Shmuel said’: although it is true that he was Rav Hisda's pupil, as is evident in the first chapter of Bava Batra 12b, Nevertheless, the exchange across Bava Kamma 20a–b is difficult. Rav Hisda asked Rami bar Hama a question. Rami said, ‘It is a Mishnah.’ Rav Hisda asked which one. Rami said, ‘I will not tell you until you serve me.’ Rav Hisda took his scarf and wrapped it around him. Rami then told him which Mishnah. The gloss says Rava was jealous. Rava said, ‘How little the man worries or notices,’ etc., because the cases did not correspond, etc. (Sukkah 29, beginning of a: Rabbah bar Hama; in my view a scribal error for Rami bar Hama.) When they stood before Rav Hisda, they ran through the received text together and then examined the reasoning. The passage is attested at Sukkah 29a [the Ketubbot locator נדה ב remains unresolved]. Heilprin’s Pesahim 27b witness reads R' Ammi bar Hama. Heilprin takes the forms to name one person and proposes a scribal error. The checked text reads Rami bar Hama. R' Yosef bar Hama disagrees with him. He transmitted in R' Yitzhak’s name. Rav Yitzhak bar Rav Yehudah studied with him, then went before Rav Sheshet. He spoke to R' Yirmeyah of Difti. Also Rav Kahana. He did not include Rav Menashya bar Tahlifa in the invitation to bless; Rava said he died young for not including him (see there). In Hullin 35a, Rav Yitzhak bar Shmuel bar Marta spoke before Rav Nahman, and Rami bar Hama raised an objection. He spoke to Rav Nahman: Bava Kamma 106a; He challenged Rav Nahman in Bava Metzia 65a and Eruvin 34b. The checked passages also give alternate attributions to Rav Ukva bar Hama and Rav Ukva bar Abba, respectively. He transmitted in Rav Nahman’s name (Gittin 39b). Also Rav Safra. His brother Rav Ukva likewise married Rav Hisda's daughter (see there). Rav Amram. Beitzah 29b tells how Rav Ashi’s wife sifted flour. Rav Ashi said, ‘My wife is Rami bar Hama’s daughter. Rami bar Hama was a master of practice. Had she not seen it in her father’s house,’ etc. Heilprin adds that he was meticulous in his conduct. In Asheri, Rami bar Hama regularly attended Rav Pappa. Rif reads Rav Pappi, a master of practice. The passage continues, ‘Had she not seen it in her father’s house,’ etc. This is puzzling, since it is not mentioned in the Gemara. I have also not found anywhere in the Talmud that Rami bar Hama was before Rav Pappa. Ta’anit 9a reads, “Rami bar Hama said in Rav’s name.” She'erit Yosef counted him among Rav's pupils; this needs examination, since he died young in Rava's days, as above, and was Rava's contemporary, as evident in Bava Batra 12b: Rav Hisda's daughter sat in her father's lap, while Rami bar Hama and Rava sat there. He asked her, ‘Which of them do you want?’ She answered, ‘Both,’ and Rava said, ‘And I last.’ So it happened: he married her ten years after Rami bar Hama's death (see there). Rava was born on the day Rav Yehudah, Rav's pupil, died. How could Rami bar Hama be Rav's pupil? Heilprin found the same teaching attributed to Rami bar Rav in Makkot 23b and in his Shabbat 32b witness. The checked Shabbat text gives both Rav and Hama. Ta’anit 9a reads Rami bar Hama. Thus the Ta'anit Gemara misled She'erit Yosef, who did not consider that Ta'anit has a scribal error. Rava said of him, ‘As sharp as he is, so great is his error’ (Bava Metzia 96b). Heilprin attributes “Because of his sharpness, he did not examine it” to Rava. In the checked Eruvin 90a the phrase appears in the ensuing discussion, after a statement by Rabbah. Rava married his wife (see there). He was sharp-witted, and all his days Rabbah challenged him. I do not know where Rabbah challenged him. Rabbah bar bar Hana arranged a match for his son in Rav Shmuel bar Katina’s household. In the same passage, Rami bar Hama responds to Rav Hisda (Berakhot 47a). The checked text gives Rav Shmuel bar Rav Katina. He challenged Rav Shmuel bar Yitzhak bar Marta (the checked Hullin 35a has Rav Yitzhak bar Shmuel bar Marta). He transmitted in Resh Lakish’s name: Menahot 35b; Avodah Zarah 45a. Rav Sheshet raised an objection that Rami bar Hama praised. The ensuing discussion was sent to R' Abba bar Zavda (Bava Metzia 16a). He applied the verse to Rav Sheshet, ‘David laid these matters to heart’ (Shevuot 45b).
